text.p: Australian Internet service provider OzEmail Ltd said on Tuesday it plans to offer local advertising on the Internet and allow advertisers to target specific groups through its joint venture with satellite television company British Sky Broadcasting.
The two companies announced the joint venture last week, saying global advertising revenue on the Internet was expected to exceed US$5 billion by the turn of the century.
The venture will be launched in New York on December 3.

The main plank of the project would be to offer advertising targetted at local audiences on Web sites anywhere in the world, OzEmail chief executive Sean Howard told reporters at a third quarter results briefing. "Most advertising in the world is regionally based but unless you can capture that opportunity, you are constantly going to restrict yourself, as the Internet has done, to global advertisers," Howard said.
Australian users, for example, spent 90 percent of their time surfing the net on sites outside Australia, limiting the number of sites available to Australian advertisers, he said.
Under the joint venture's proposal, an Australian user accessing a German Web site would see an Australian advertisement, while a French user visiting the same site would see a French advertisement.
"Regional advertising is a keystone," Howard said. "Beyond that you want to be able to further segment the audience."
OzEmail is working with a control group of about 200,000 Internet users in the U.S. for whom demographic information was available, he said.

When a new site was added to the Web, visits by members of the control group would be monitored to build a picture of the sex, age and socio-economic group of users attracted to certain sites. The venture could then profile other users who visited the same sites, eventually building a profile of Internet users.

These additional users would only be identified by their Internet code number. "If we found a user, for example, who visited a lot of motor car sites ... if they lived in Germany we might show them an advertisement for BMW," Howard said.
OzEmail managing director David Spence said the company had been working on the project for five months, and should be able to offer the service shortly after its formal launch.

Howard said the venture planned to have offices in New York, London and Los Angeles by the end of the year, and one or more Asian offices and one or more European offices by the first quarter of 1997.
The two companies said last week they would put an equal amount into the venture. Howard declined to give details but said OzEmail's contribution would be "well into seven figures".
